title: Morgan Stanley Hikes S&P 500 Target to 8,300 on AI Boom - Yahoo Finance
text: Morgan Stanley Hikes S&P 500 Target to 8,300 on AI Boom Nauman Khan May 15, 2026 1 min read MS ^GSPC HSBA.L This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Morgan Stanley raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 to 8,000 from 7,800 and set a 12-month view of 8,300, saying resilient profits and faster AI adoption could keep the U.S. rally going. The firm now expects S&P 500 companies to earn $339 a share in 2026, which would mark 23% growth from a year earlier. Its strategists said the call is built more on earnings strength and operating leverage than on higher valuation multiples. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 9 Warning Signs with CSCO. Is SPY fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. The outlook followed a strong first-quarter reporting season. By May 8, 440 S&P 500 companies had posted results, and 83.2% had beaten earnings estimates, according to LSEG data cited in the report. Other firms have also turned more constructive. HSBC recently lifted its year-end target to 7,650 from 7,500, while Yardeni Research raised its outlook to 8,250 from 7,700, both pointing to durable earnings momentum.
